text.p: The biggest commercial bank in the Baltics, Estonia's Hansapank, plans to establish itself in Lithuania this year, the newspaper Verslo Zinios reported on Wednesday.
The newspaper quoted a representative of Hansapank, Juri Mois, as saying that Hansapank is analysing the operations of several Lithuanian banks.
He said Hansapank is waiting until the Lithuanian government announces the privatisation conditions of the Lithuanian Agricultural Bank and the State Commercial Bank.
Mois was also quoted as saying that if Hansapank alone does not succeed in buying into one of those two banks, its biggest shareholders might participate.
Hansapank's biggest shareholders include Merita Bank Ltd., AS Flotten, Bank of Bermuda and Hoiupank.
The head of the Agricultural Bank's treasury department, Valdas Bernatavichius, told the newspaper that Hansapank was among the potential investors who showed the biggest interest in the bank.
Bernatavichius was also quoted as saying that if Hansapank fails to participate in the privatisation of the two banks, it intends to open a representative office in Lithuania.
"The Estonian market has become too small and that's why they are looking for new markets," Bernatavichius was quoted by the newspaper as saying.
